subject: Biochemistry
vignette: A 3-month-old infant has hypotonia, seizures, and hepatomegaly with dysmorphic facies and jaundice. Plasma very-long-chain fatty acids and pipecolic acid are elevated, and liver biopsy shows a marked absence of peroxisomes.
question: Which of the following metabolic processes is most directly impaired by the organelle defect in this patient?

options.text: Peroxisomal beta-oxidation of very-long-chain fatty acids
Cholesterol synthesis in the smooth endoplasmic reticulum

explanation_correct: This infant has Zellweger syndrome, an autosomal recessive failure of peroxisome biogenesis caused by PEX gene mutations. Peroxisomes perform the beta-oxidation of very-long-chain fatty acids and the alpha-oxidation of branched-chain fatty acids, so these fatty acids accumulate and cause the neurologic and hepatic manifestations.

explanation_incorrect.A: Mitochondria, not peroxisomes, carry out beta-oxidation of long-chain fatty acids such as palmitate, which remains intact in Zellweger syndrome.
explanation_incorrect.C: Fatty acid synthesis takes place in the cytosol and is not a peroxisomal process.
explanation_incorrect.D: Ketogenesis occurs in hepatic mitochondria and is not directly impaired by loss of peroxisomes.
explanation_incorrect.E: Cholesterol synthesis occurs in the cytosol and smooth endoplasmic reticulum, not in peroxisomes.

educationalObjective: Peroxisomes are required for beta-oxidation of very-long-chain fatty acids, and defective peroxisome biogenesis causes Zellweger syndrome.
